newsitem.title: POLAND: HSBC James Capel values NFI units at PLN 162.
newsitem.headline: HSBC James Capel values NFI units at PLN 162.

text.p: NFI units in Poland's mass privatisation programme are fairly valued at 162 zlotys using an enterprise value/sales valuation for each NFI based on listed Warsaw bourse sectors, HSBC James Capel said.

"Although we estimate the value of one privatisation certificate at 162 zlotys, the double discount mechanism used in the valuation process may be viewed as conservative," HSBC James Capel said in a report dated June 17.
"Without these discounts the value of one privatisation certificate would be as high as 283 zlotys," it added.

HSBC James Capel said that based on efficiency adjustments and perceived management ability to add value, NIFs 1, Progress, Magna Polonia, Piast and Zachodni were the most attractive funds and were recommended buys.
It said NFIs 3, Octava, Foksal, 11, Fortuna and Hetman had a positive outlook while NFIs 2, Victoria, Kazimierz Wielki and E. Kwiatkowski were affected by uncertainty.
Under the Polish government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.

From May 12, the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme have been entitled to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which started trade on the Warsaw bourse on June 12. Each NFI has 31,026,185 shares.
The units, which closed on the bourse on Tuesday at 141.5 zlotys, lose their validity on December 31, 1998.

HSBC James Capel said that though the new NFI share market provided market benchmarks for each fund, high price volatility due to low liquidity and speculation meant fair value would not always be reflected.

It said that for more precise recommendations to be made more information would be needed such as financial statements for the underlying companies, realistic cash flow forecasts and a greater number of transactions.
